titleHtml: Improving PFAS Water Treatment through AI-Supported Engineering Design
bodyHtml: CMU Engineering featured Prof. Pingbo Tang and collaborators' work on AI-supported engineering design for PFAS water treatment systems. The project uses digital twins, human-AI collaboration, and analysis of design-team communication to help water utilities move more quickly from concept to deployable infrastructure.

titleHtml: Ava Jahan Biglari Selected as Pennsylvania’s Student Representative for the IHEEP Conference
bodyHtml: Ava was selected as Pennsylvania’s student representative for the IHEEP Conference in Austin, Texas, recognizing her research on heavy-duty vehicle safety through perception-to-risk modeling.

titleHtml: Miaosi Dong Awarded the Presidential Fellowship in the College of Engineering
bodyHtml: Miaosi was awarded the Presidential Fellowship in the College of Engineering, a competitive $55,000 award recognizing her outstanding academic achievement and research excellence.

titleHtml: Seongeun Park Awarded the Claire and John Bertucci Fellowship in Engineering
bodyHtml: Seongeun was awarded the Claire and John Bertucci Fellowship in Engineering, a full-tuition fellowship recognizing her academic excellence and promising research.

titleHtml: Cheng Zhang’s ENG-DRB Dataset
bodyHtml: ENG-DRB is a discourse relation dataset built specifically for engineering content, introduced in a recent paper at IJCNLP-AACL 2025. The dataset analyzes over 1,200 relations extracted from real tutorial videos across civil, mechanical, and electrical engineering and shows that even advanced AI models struggle to accurately understand engineering discourse, particularly implicit causal and temporal relations. This work highlights a gap between general-purpose NLP and the specialized language used by engineers. The dataset and code are open-source and publicly available.

titleHtml: Prof. Pingbo Tang Appointed as Director of the Engineers’ Society of Western Pennsylvania (ESWP)
bodyHtml: We are pleased to share that Prof. Pingbo Tang has been appointed as a Director of the Engineers’ Society of Western Pennsylvania (ESWP).

titleHtml: Human–AI Collaboration in Industrialized Building Systems
bodyHtml: Our work on human–AI collaboration for safe and efficient production of building mechanical system components and modular housing units was featured on the Autodesk Research Blog. The project is supported by the Pennsylvania Department of Community & Economic Development, with industry partners DMI Companies, Inc. and Module Design, and collaborators Burcu Akinci, Yorie Nakahira, Ruoxin Xiong, Xiyu Deng, Miaosi Dong, Joonsun Hwang, Yanyu Wang, Haoming Jing, and Yael Netser.

titleHtml: Prof. Pingbo Tang Wins Engineering Faculty Award
bodyHtml: Safety21 researcher Prof. Pingbo Tang was selected for a 2025 Engineering faculty award. He received the Steven J. Fenves Award for Systems Research.

titleHtml: Seongeun Park Receives the CUAHSI Hydroinformatics Innovation Fellowship
bodyHtml: Seongeun was selected for the CUAHSI Hydroinformatics Innovation Fellowship, supported by NSF. Her project applies AI methods to strengthen training and decision-making in remote infrastructure operations through virtual AI avatars.

titleHtml: Accelerating Safe Microreactor Deployment with AI-Powered Knowledge
bodyHtml: Our research group is developing AI-powered frameworks to support the safe and efficient deployment of nuclear microreactors. The approach uses large language models and knowledge graphs to align procedures, regulations, and training across different countries.

titleHtml: HMHI Research Featured at One Water Summit 2025
bodyHtml: Jinfeng Lou, Shambhavi Jilkar, Zijie Liang, and Gina Im, led by Prof. Pingbo Tang, presented HMHI’s work on human–AI collaboration in water systems and infrastructure operations in changing environments. The project is supported by the Carnegie Bosch Institute, with special thanks to Dr. Yuxin Zhang for the collaboration.

titleHtml: Pengkun Liu’s Research Featured by NSF ACCESS and PSC
bodyHtml: Pengkun’s bridge inspection research was featured by the Pittsburgh Supercomputing Center. The project uses VR simulation and AI to improve training and consistency in bridge inspections, addressing infrastructure safety challenges.

titleHtml: Graduation Celebration
bodyHtml: We celebrated the achievements of our graduating members: Kahyun completed her postdoctoral research, Pengkun earned his Ph.D., and Zijie and Tiantian graduated with their M.S. degrees. Congratulations to all!

titleHtml: Seongeun Park Awarded the Chishiki AI Fellowship
bodyHtml: Seongeun was awarded the Chishiki AI Fellowship in Civil Engineering, hosted by UT Austin with support from NSF and CII. Her research explores how AI can capture and share tacit knowledge from experienced workers to improve trust in training and decision-making.

titleHtml: Presentation at 2025 Manufacturing PA Innovation Program Expo
bodyHtml: Miaosi Dong, Joonsun Hwang and Prof. Pingbo Tang participated in the 2025 Manufacturing PA Innovation Program Expo, hosted by Harrisburg University of Science & Technology. The event, supported by the Pennsylvania Department of Community & Economic Development, brought together faculty, students, and industry partners to showcase emerging technologies in Pennsylvania manufacturing. HMHI Lab presented ongoing research on integrating AI and human intelligence to enhance workforce development and process optimization in HVAC manufacturing systems.

titleHtml: Presentations at I3CE 2025
bodyHtml: Pengkun, Ava, Joonsun, Zijie, Tiantian presented their research at the 2025 International Conference on Computing in Civil Engineering (I3CE). Their work spans topics such as drone-assisted inspection, vehicle inspection training, personalized learning in modular construction, human-AI collaboration, and reducing production waste.

titleHtml: Ava Jahan Biglari Presents Research to U.S. Secretary Pete Buttigieg
bodyHtml: Ava presented her research on improving vehicle inspections to former U.S. Secretary of Transportation Pete Buttigieg during his recent visit to Pittsburgh. Her project combines human expertise and advanced technologies to ultimately make our roads safer.

titleHtml: Miaosi Dong Awarded Liang Ji-Dan Graduate Fellowship
bodyHtml: Miaosi  has been awarded the prestigious Liang Ji-Dan Graduate Fellowship in recognition of her outstanding academic achievements and research contributions. Her current research focuses on enhancing worker guidance in customized HVAC component manufacturing by integrating human expertise and machine intelligence. Through explainable AI and human-knowledge-guided Bayesian optimization, she aims to reduce setup waste and improve collaboration in complex production systems.

titleHtml: Jinfeng Lou Featured as CBI Fellow
bodyHtml: Jinfeng was selected as a 2024 CBI Fellow by the Carnegie Bosch Institute. His fellowship research focuses on developing AI systems that adapt to rapidly changing urban environments, with a specific focus on subway flood resilience. The fellowship is co-hosted by Professors Pingbo Tang and Cleotilde Gonzalez at Carnegie Mellon University.

titleHtml: Empowering Civil Engineering with Generative AI Workshop
bodyHtml: Prof. Pingbo Tang, Prof. Beibei Li (Heinz College), Ruoxin Xiong, Yael Netser, and Joonsun Hwang organized a workshop titled "Empowering Civil Engineering with Generative AI: Opportunities, Risks, and Future Directions" at the ASCE i3CE 2024 Conference. The session addressed GAI’s impact on AEC workflows, ethical concerns, and future directions through talks and breakout discussions.

titleHtml: Ensuring a Future With Clean Water
bodyHtml: Pengkun Liu was highlighted by NSF’s ACCESS program for creating a virtual water treatment plant using PSC’s Bridges‑2 supercomputer. His simulation enables risk‑free testing of scenarios—from emergencies to equipment upgrades—preserving senior engineers’ expertise and speeding up trainee education. “We rely on powerful GPUs for both VR rendering and AI model training,” Liu notes. This work advances digital‑twin and AI methods for sustainable water infrastructure management.

titleHtml: Human-AI Know-How Share for H2O Treatment
bodyHtml: Pengkun Liu leveraged PSC’s Bridges‑2 GPUs to build a virtual water‑treatment plant that learns from veteran engineers’ responses to simulated breakdowns. His AI achieved a 0.712 recall in fault identification (versus 0.851 for experts), and together human‑AI recall rose to 0.885. Next, Liu plans to use this VR environment to train new engineers, creating a scalable human‑AI co‑learning system for sustainable water infrastructure.
